sections.h2: What Florida weather does to a Lake City deck
body: Lying flat and fully exposed, a deck takes the brunt of every sunny afternoon and every downpour, so it wears out ahead of the siding, the fence, and the roof. Ultraviolet light eats the top layer of the boards and leaves them silver. Rainwater wicks into cut ends and around every screw. On low, shady decks, green growth turns the walking surface slippery. Most of the decks we stain in Lake City subdivisions show all three by the time the owner calls. Good deck staining in Lake City, FL undoes the damage you can see and slows the decay you cannot.

Stain will not save a soft board. Before we quote a stain job, the crew lead probes boards, stair treads, and rail posts and notes anything that needs replacing. Want to look before we arrive? Our deck rot warning signs post shows the same spots our crew lead checks with a screwdriver.

Old stain that is peeling or flaking has to come off. Peeling film traps water, and new stain can't soak in through it. Once stripped and washed, the boards dry out, then get sanded to knock down fuzzy grain and the last of the silver layer. Next comes a penetrating stain. Anywhere it is sprayed, a brush follows right behind to push the stain down between boards and deep into the pores instead of leaving it sitting on top.

sections.h2: Choosing opacity and planning around the weather
body: Clear-toned stains let the wood pattern show through, at the cost of an earlier recoat. Solid-color stain covers flaws and lasts longer, though it behaves closer to paint. Most Lake City owners settle on semi-transparent as the compromise. Because stain only takes on bone-dry boards with no rain coming, the cooler months from fall into spring are the easy window; in July and August we stain early and watch the radar all morning.

Odds are the fence around the yard is just as gray. We can stain it in the same tone through our Lake City fence painting and staining service. Background on products and methods is on the company-wide deck and fence stain page, and our Lake City overview covers the rest of our local work.

faqs.q: How often does a Lake City deck need restaining?
faqs.a: That comes down to how much sun the boards get and how opaque the stain is, with clear-toned products wearing through faster than solids. During the walkthrough, we look at how the current finish has worn and recommend an opacity based on that.

faqs.q: Is it OK to put new stain on top of what is there now?
faqs.a: Only when the existing finish is intact and the wood still drinks it in. If it is peeling, we strip it off, because fresh stain cannot get through a failing film.

faqs.q: Will you fix spongy boards and loose stair treads?
faqs.a: We will. Bad boards, treads, and popped screws are flagged on the site visit and priced in the quote, then fixed before any stain goes down.

faqs.q: Which months work best for staining a Lake City deck?
faqs.a: October into spring. Humidity drops, boards dry faster after a shower, and those 3 p.m. storms mostly take a break. Summer jobs are done in the mornings, and only after the wood has dried out from the last rain.
